description: Resiliency Officer Helps Design An Environmental Impact Bond To Finance Community Resilience Projects is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Chesapeake Bay Foundation. Hampton's Resiliency Officer led the development of Virginia's first ever Environmental Impact Bond to help finance community resilience projects. The bond enables impact investors to support projects that provide resilience outcomes for a community. Coverage: Virginia (2022). The toolkit gives Virginia as the location, 2022 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.

outcomes: Hampton's Resiliency Officer led the development of Virginia's first ever Environmental Impact Bond to help finance community resilience projects. The bond enables impact investors to support innovative projects that provide resilience outcomes for a community. The bond was designed to finance projects that will reduce stormwater runoff and provide multiple layered public benefits to the community.
